prompt:
You run weekly onboarding A/B tests. Here is every finished test so far: what you predicted
and what was measured.

- round 1: Preset Customization Fallback Flow [adoption, new_flow]: predicted +10.0%, measured +8.0% (p=0.005557), won
- round 1: Interactive Wait Screen Tips & Status [home, wait_info]: predicted +12.0%, measured +5.1% (p=0.016429), won
- round 1: Account Sync & Cloud Reassurance Warning [sign_in, hint]: predicted +4.0%, measured +0.2% (p=0.910329), lost: no clear effect
- round 1: Desktop Visibility Guidance Copy Update [finish, copy]: predicted +6.0%, measured +5.9% (p=0.118574), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Pet Personality Spotlight Redesign [adoption, redesign]: predicted +8.0%, measured -3.8% (p=0.148295), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Desktop Launcher Verification Screen [finish, new_screen]: predicted +2.0%, measured -5.6% (p=0.118998), lost: no clear effect
- round 2: Live Generation Progress Bar with Mascot [home, wait_info]: predicted +5.0%, measured +0.6% (p=0.745981), lost: no clear effect

Previous lessons:
Adding fallback flows during adoption (new_flow) was helpful (+8.0%), though the predicted +10.0% was slightly too high.
Interactive wait screen tips and status updates (wait_info) were helpful (+5.1%), but the predicted +12.0% significantly overestimated the impact.
Account sync reassurance warnings and hints at sign-in showed no clear effect (+0.2%).
Copy updates at the finish step showed no clear effect, despite leaning positive (+5.9%, p=0.119).

Rewrite the lessons: at most 6 short rules about which kinds of change worked, which did not, and
where your predictions were too high or too low. Call a kind of change helpful only if a test of that
kind won (was significant); for tests with no clear effect, say no effect was seen, even if the numbers
lean one way. Keep rules that still hold, drop ones the data contradicts. Return JSON {"lessons": ["..."]}

lessons: Fallback flows during adoption (new_flow) were helpful (+8.0%), though the +10.0% prediction was slightly overestimated.
Interactive wait screen tips (wait_info) were helpful (+5.1%), but adding a progress bar with mascot to the wait screen showed no clear effect.
Sign-in reassurance hints and copy updates at the finish step showed no clear effect.
Adoption step redesigns and new verification screens at the finish step showed no clear effect.
Predictions consistently overestimate the actual measured impact across tests.
